learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to explain the state of the art in agricultural machinery, and to identify, determine, and explain the functional and process chains used, as well as the partial and overall functions.

Students can classify and evaluate real machines and further developments according to technical and economic criteria. They are able to select machines for specific applications (e.g., depending on a specific soil type or a specific crop) and can make reasoned decisions for the further development of pre-developed prototypes.
Students can summarize the contents of essential regulations and describe test methods. They can evaluate, structure, and present determined data.
Students present their elaborated results in a written report and a presentation.

Students understand the different boundary conditions for analyzing the overall system 'human-tractor-implement-soil-plant'. They can identify suitable machines, assemblies, components, and procedures and develop and discuss appropriate applications with regard to technical, ergonomic, and social challenges.

Graduates can apply knowledge and understanding to professional activities and develop or further develop solutions in the application of agricultural machinery. This includes the application and activation of acquired knowledge, a critical understanding of knowledge, and a methodical expansion of knowledge.

Graduates derive and define research questions from the field of agricultural machinery technology and the use of agricultural technology. They explain and justify the operationalization of research and apply research methods, present and explain research results.
Students present their results, elaborated in cooperation within the project group, in a written report and a presentation in a clearly structured form.

Graduates develop a professional self-image that is oriented towards the goals and standards of professional action in professional fields primarily outside of science; they justify their own professional actions with theoretical and methodical knowledge and can assess their own abilities, autonomously reflect on subject-related design and decision-making freedoms and use them under guidance. They recognize situationally appropriate framework conditions for professional action and can ethically justify their decisions. They critically reflect on their professional actions in relation to societal expectations and consequences.

syllabus_topics: History and socio-economic and societal framework conditions of agricultural production
Overview of machines used in field work for:
Harvest (grain, forage, and root crop harvesting)
Material properties of soils and agricultural goods
Typical machine elements and assemblies in agricultural machinery and systems
Use of electronics in agricultural machines/ISOBUS
assessment_rules: The graded assessment consists of a term paper (approx. 10-25 pages) and a presentation (20 minutes plus approx. 10 minutes discussion).
